newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers rise, rest of Europe stable.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers rise, rest of Europe stable.

text.p: ARA fuel oil bunkers rose on Monday, but other areas were slow to follow, with activity only in isolated ports, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 cst fuel oil rose $2 a tonne as barge prices firmed, with stored material trading at $126 fob and refinery product at $128 fob. Suppliers said refined product was in particularly short supply and majors were holding back, waiting for further strength later in the week.
"There's more of the stored (fuel oil), originally from Russia, but it has a water content too high for some tastes," one trader said.
The ARA market was quiet as ship owners were reluctant to buy, despite many traders' expectations of yet higher prices.
Hamburg was steady at around $127 fob, but, despite being on a par with Rotterdam, trading was very slow.
Mediterranean prices were broadly steady. Most places were quiet, but deferrals from last week led to healthy business in some Spanish ports.
Fujairah fuel oil prices were also barely changed. Enquiries for the end of the week were promising, traders said.
Durban fuel oil was steady at $130/$131 ex-wharf.
